title: Inheritance and Initialization Safety
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of inheritance and initialization safety using at least one correct term from the lesson.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Inheritance and Initialization Safety** as part of **Inheritance, Interfaces, and Polymorphism**. Use interfaces and inheritance when they express substitutability, and prefer composition when an object should contain or coordinate collaborators. Use the subtopics—Base-Class Initialization Order, Calling Overridable Members During Initialization, Avoiding Initialization Hazards—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

items.title: Base-Class Initialization Order
items.text: Base-Class Initialization Order should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.
